 Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb.,

Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. Ravindra Nagappa Markal
 S/o Nagappa Markal,
 Aged about 33 years,
 Residing at:
 Ragihaklu, Patlamane,
 Shivamogga, Karnataka-577 415.
 (By Sri. T. Manjunatha, Adv.,)
 Vs.
Respondent/s: 1. M/s Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
 Motor Claims Hub, 
 No.5/4, 3rd Floor, S. V. Arcade,
 Bilekehalli, IIM Post,
 Bannerghatta Road, 
 Bangalore-560 076. 
 (Policy No.215066/31/19/016387  Valid Upto 20.10.2018 to 19.10.2023) 
 (By Sri. M. A. Patil, Adv.)
 2. Sri. Sagar prakash Chaudhari  S/o Prakash Ratan,
 Plot No.31, 1st Floor,
 Sector-06, Koperhairane,
 Navi Mumbai,
 SCCH-21 2 MVC No.5159/2023  Maharashtra-400709.

Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
1 Date of institution of the : 04.08.2023 petition Nature of the Petition : U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act Date of commencement of : 19.08.2024 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 25.11.2024 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s  01 03 21  JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 13.07.2023.
2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 13.07.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 53-HK-4418 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding near Ramamurthy Nagar Signal, Ramamurthy Nagar, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
MH-43-BQ-2028 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner. 
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. 
Immediately, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as Delivery Boy at Swiggy and Zomato and earning Rs.60,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. 
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
2 conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134, 170 and 149(2) of M. V.
Act. The petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident. He also denied the age,
occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. MH-43-BQ-2028 on 13.07.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., near Ramamurthy Nagar Signa, Ramamurthy Nagar,
Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that he is not liable to pay compensation as pleaded in the written statement? 
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.17 and also examined Dr. Krishan Prasad as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.18 to 23 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents. 
6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under;
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Negative, Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following: 
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition. He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17. Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar,
Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 & 6 are the IMV Reports, Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate, 
Ex.P.8 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.9 is the Reply notice, Ex.P.10 is the Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
3 Charge sheet, Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 are the Discharge Summaries, Ex.P.14 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.15 is the Bank account extract, Ex.P.16 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card and Ex.P.17 is the Notarized copy of Driving License.
10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 13.07.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HK-4418 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding near Ramamurthy Nagar Signal, Ramamurthy Nagar, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. MH-43-BQ- 2028 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner. Due to which,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient. Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.216/2023. After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 337 of IPC along with section 134(B), 187, 115 and 177 of M. V. Act.
11. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. MH-43-BQ-2028.
12. As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "
The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt,
as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ". 
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the K. R. Puram Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2. On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 216/2023. The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14. During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of riding by the rider of offending motorcycle. The Ex.P.3 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.4 (Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the rider of motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC along with section 134(B), 187, 115 and 177 of M. V. Act. The Ex.P.5 & 6 i.e.,
certified copy of the IMV Reports discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
4 mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place. By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-07-N-0928. Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative. 
17. ISSUE No.2: The learned advocate for insurance company argued that, insured vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident and petitioner has given complaint on the next day of accident. 
Further he argued that, in order to implicate the insured vehicle petitioner has given complaint on next day of the alleged accident. But in order to support his contention insurance company has not produced any documents before this court. Further, despite issuance of notice owner of the offending vehicle/insured vehicle remained absent before this court. Moreover, as per the records accident taken place on 13.07.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., As per Ex.P.1 bother of the petitioner has given first information to the K. R. Puram Traffic Police on 14.07.2023 at 3.00 p.m., So, petitioner's brother has filed the case within a day. In these type of accidents injured usually take treatment at first then think about filing of the complaint before police. As stated above, insurance company has not adduced any evidence. 
Further, learned advocate for insurance company argued that, respondent No.2 has committed offence as per the Motor Vehicles Act, hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in the alleged accident. But in this case, respondent No.1 insurance company has not produced any documents in order to show that, rider of the offending vehicle violated the terms of insurance policy. Hence, this court opine that, insurance company failed to prove that, he is not liable to pay compensation and there is no delay in filing of the complaint. Accordingly, I answer this Issue in the Negative. 
18. ISSUE No.3: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, wherein he was admitted was inpatient and he took treatment. 
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING: In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital as an inpatient from 14.07.2023 to 15.07.2023 and then from 27.07.2023 to 31.07.2023 and again from 31.08.2023 to 01.09.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore for 06 days. He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained Left proximal Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
5 Tibia- comminuted fracture, Right foot-open comminuted fracture of 2nd & 5th, Right foot-4th &
5th EDL Tendom Tear and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature. Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience. 
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering. 
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 30 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.2,38,396/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,38,396/-
towards medical expenses. 
21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 Discharge summaries issued by Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 14.07.2023 to 15.07.2023 and then from 27.07.2023 to 31.07.2023 and again from 31.08.2023 to 01.09.2023 i.e. for 06 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Delivery boy at Swiggy and Zomato and earning Rs.60,000/- per month, in support of his income he has produced the bank statement. But on perusal of the bank statement it is very difficult for the tribunal to assess the income of the petitioner. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2023. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/-
under this head. 
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Krishan Prasad in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total physical disability of lower limb at 58% and that of whole body disability at 20%. Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor. Same was admitted by the PW.2 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.2 reads as follows :
"I have not personally treated the petitioner."
Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
6 He was sworn that, petitioner has got 20% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability. However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 10% of disability to the petitioner. 
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined. 
Ex.P.16 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 11.09.1990 and accident took place in the year 2023. Accordingly, I assess his age as 33 years at the time of this accident. As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '16'. Hence Rs.16,000 X 12 X 16 X 10% = 3,07,200/-. Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.3,07,200/-. 
24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 14.07.2023 to 15.07.2023 and then from 27.07.2023 to 31.07.2023 and again from 31.08.2023 to 01.09.2023 i.e., 06 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. 
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works. He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. 
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness. 
26. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses. The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.80,000/- and further deposed that, petitioner needs daily application of vaseline of his large skin graft areas which will cost Rs.7,000/- annually. 
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital. Hence, under this head Rs.25,000/- is awarded. 
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 2,38,396/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/-
Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
7 up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 3,07,200/-
Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
loss of happiness. 
7 Future Medical Expenses Rs. 25,000/-
Total Rs. 6,70,596/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,70,596/- under various heads. 
27. LIABILITY: As discussed in issue No.1 and 2, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. MH-43-BQ-2028 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said rider of the offending vehicle. From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 20.10.2018 to 19.10.2023. Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 13.07.2023. Hence,
policy was in force at the time of accident. Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner. 
28. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative. 
29. ISSUE No.4: In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,70,596/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization. 
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two Ravindra Nagappa Markal vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87114808/
8 months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon. 
 Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019. 
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court. 
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. 
Draw award accordingly. 
[Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and then corrected by me and pronounced in the open court on this the 25th Day of November-2024) 
(VIJAYKUMAR S. HIREMATH) XVII ADDL. JUDGE, Court of Small Causes &
Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru.
